successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy entity is defined with the exact canonical fields (id, policyName, leaveType, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt), with the optional numeric fields typed `number | undefined` (never null).

The repository exposes the canonical method set findById, findByLeaveType, findActive, create, update; write methods (create, update) accept an optional PoolClient as the last parameter and read methods use the shared pool.
create persists a row via parameterized SQL and returns the mapped entity with a generated id and createdAt/updatedAt timestamps; update persists only supplied changes and returns the updated entity.
findById returns the mapped entity or null on a miss; update on a missing id throws a typed PolicyNotFoundError; a pg 23505 violation is mapped to a typed UniqueConstraintError.
The service is a thin delegating facade over an injectable repository (defaulting to the concrete repository) and does not import the pool or issue SQL directly.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/policy/ covering the repository (mocking the shared pool), the service (injecting a mock repository), and the error types, and the suite passes under `npm run build && npx jest`.

constraints: No `any` — use `unknown` with type guards (HARNESS.json constraint `no-any`).
All database access goes through the repository layer only — no inline SQL or pool import in the service (GP-001 / `no-direct-db-outside-repository`).
Strict TypeScript with `tsc --noEmit` passing; no implicit any, strict null checks.
Repository queries use raw `pg` parameterized SQL against the shared pool — no Knex in queries (Knex is migrations-only).
Optional numeric fields are typed `number | undefined` (not null), per the task specification.

The policy module has no multi-table transaction; the service does not need IUnitOfWork, and no repository method wraps a transaction (withTransaction lives only in the data-access layer, never on a repository).
outOfScope: No controller, routes, or HTTP surface for the policy module — API exposure and RBAC wiring are deferred to later phases (leave controller/routes, auth).

No audit-record emission from the policy service in this phase — GP-002 audit wiring for state-changing operations is handled by the leave module's transactional flow, not by the policy module itself.
No DDL/migrations for the leave_policies table — the conceptual table mapping is documented only; schema creation is out of scope for this phase.
No IUnitOfWork usage in the policy service — policy has no multi-table transaction; transaction orchestration belongs to the leave module (Phase 8).

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle states are ACTIVE and INACTIVE, expressed via the boolean `isActive`; a policy is created with a caller-supplied `isActive` and may be toggled via update. `id`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` are generated by the repository and never caller-supplied.

`leaveType` must be a valid LeaveType enum value; `entitlementDays` is a required non-negative number; the optional numeric fields (accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays) are `number | undefined` and, when present, are persisted as their numeric value (undefined maps to NULL in the row).
The conceptual table `leave_policies` uses snake_case columns with PK `id` and indexes on `leave_type` and `is_active`; there is no `deleted_at` column (policies are not soft-deleted).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists a new policy and returns the mapped entity with generated id/createdAt/updatedAt. Accepts an optional PoolClient as the last parameter to join a caller's transaction; falls back to the shared pool when omitted. A pg 23505 violation is mapped to a typed UniqueConstraintError.

Persists only the supplied changes and returns the updated entity. Accepts an optional PoolClient as the last parameter. Throws a typed PolicyNotFoundError when no row matches the id; maps pg 23505 to UniqueConstraintError.
Read-only; uses the shared pool (no client parameter). Returns the mapped entity or null when absent.
Read-only; uses the shared pool. Returns all policies matching the given LeaveType (empty array when none).
Read-only; uses the shared pool. Returns only policies where isActive is true (empty array when none).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Import the LeaveType enum from the shared types module (via its public entry point) — do not redefine it. The enum exposes annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity.
Import the shared `pg` Pool from the shared db module (via its public entry point) for all repository queries; never construct a new Pool.

Mirror the committed employee module conventions: model file defines the entity plus CreateLeavePolicyInput/UpdateLeavePolicyInput; repository file defines both the I*Repository interface and the concrete class (randomUUID, mapRow, `conn = client ?? pool`, RETURNING columns); service is a thin delegating facade with an injectable repository; service interface lives in a separate I*Service file; index.ts is the public entry point exporting entity/input types, repository class+interface, service class+interface, and error types.

Reuse the established error family: a RepositoryError base with a `code` property, a PolicyNotFoundError for findById/update misses, and a UniqueConstraintError for pg code 23505 — matching the employee module's error shape and stable machine codes.
Match the canonical ILeavePolicyRepository method set (findById, findByLeaveType, findActive, create, update) and the LeavePolicy/leave_policies canonical names from the reconciled architecture.

integrationPoints.why: The LeavePolicy entity's leaveType field is typed against this enum; the policy module depends on it from Phase 1.
The repository issues raw parameterized SQL against this shared pool; the module depends on it from Phase 1.
LeaveService will consume findById/findByLeaveType/findActive to resolve entitlement and approval rules when validating leave requests against an ACTIVE policy.
